review.question: Confirm that the owner's affidavit of completion no longer shortens the clock for contracts on or after 2022-01-01, that enforcement runs one year from the last filing day for residential and commercial, and that a terminated or abandoned original contract is entered as completion_date.
review.reason: Counsel's row contradicts the statute and the VA guide on two points: it says an owner's Affidavit of Completion starts the lien clock (HB 2237 removed it; 53.052(a) counts from the month the work was 'completed, terminated, or abandoned'), and it gives 'Lien Rights Expiration: 1 Year from Date Lien Affidavit is filed - residential; 2 years - commercial' where 53.158(a) runs one year from the last day to file for both uses. Also lien_recorded and abandonment have no registry fact.

53.055(a): the filer 'must send a copy of the affidavit to the owner or reputed owner ... not later than the fifth day after the date the affidavit is filed with the county clerk'; counsel's row, 'Mail to owner w/in 5 days of filing - via trackable delivery method'; 53.003(b) governs the method. lien_recorded has no registry fact yet (SCHEMA.md §11).

The VA guide: 'HB 2237 eliminated the owner's affidavit-of-completion shortcut'; counsel's row still says 'owner can file Affidavit of Completion which starts lien deadline clock'. 53.052(a) as now written has no such trigger, so no count uses it.

Tex. Prop. Code 53.152(a) (corpus 2026-08-21): 'When a debt for labor or materials is satisfied or paid by collected funds, the person who furnished the labor or materials shall, not later than the 10th day after the date of receipt of a written request, furnish to the requesting person a release of the indebtedness and any lien claimed, to the extent of the indebtedness paid. An owner, the original contractor, or any person making the payment may request the release.'

Counsel's row, 'Release Date: w/in 10 days of final payment and written request from owner'; the VA guide, 'Within 10 days of final payment and the owner's written request.' The statute starts the clock at receipt of the request and allows the original contractor or the payer to ask, not only the owner; the release is due 'to the extent of the indebtedness paid', so a partial payment gives a partial release.

53.152(b): 'A release of lien must be in a form that would permit it to be filed of record'; counsel's row, 'Release Recorded: Yes - with same county clerk who recorded original lien', 'Lien Release Required: Yes - signed and notarized', recording format as for the lien, template 'on Texas Construction Website'. Counsel names no notarial act; acknowledgment is the recordable form and is a reviewer's call.
Counsel's row: 'Release Type of Mailing: certified or other traceable method'; no recipient role exists for the requesting party, so serve_copy is not written.
Counsel's row, 'Release Penalties: yes - no statutory penalties but Texas Fraudulent Lien Act could be used'; the statute states no consequence, so if_missed is absent and reads not_established.
53.152 was last amended in 1989 and HB 2237 did not touch it, so the cell carries no contract-date selector.

review.question: Is a release due 10 days after a written request from the owner, original contractor or payer once the debt is paid, and should the signature be an acknowledgment?
review.reason: The clock starts at the owner's, original contractor's or payer's written request (53.152(a)), and neither the demand trigger (release_demand_date) nor a requesting_party recipient is in the registry or the closed lists (SCHEMA.md §11, §14); the payment condition is not a second trigger the schema can combine with the request. Counsel's notarization wording does not name the act.
